name: Malabar Parotta
instructions: 1. Mix flour, salt, sugar, oil, and water (and egg if using) to form a soft, elastic dough, then rest for at least 1 hour.
2. Divide dough into balls, flatten thinly, and brush with oil.
3. Pleat the dough like a paper fan, roll it into a spiral (coil), and rest again for 15 minutes.
4. Gently roll out the spiral into a round disc.
5. Heat a tawa or flat griddle, cook the parotta on both sides with oil or ghee until golden brown, and clap the parotta between your hands while hot to release the layers.
description: Malabar Parotta is a culinary icon of Kerala, known for its distinct flaky, shredded texture. It is a street food staple often served with spicy meat curries like Kerala beef fry or vegetable kurma, reflecting the diverse culinary influences of the Malabar coast.
